newsitem.title: USA: Cytel files IND application for HIV vaccine.
newsitem.headline: Cytel files IND application for HIV vaccine.

text.p: Cytel Corp said on Thursday it filed an investigational new drug, or IND, application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its HIV therapeutic vaccine, known as CY2301.

If the IND is approved, Cytel said it will initiate a Phase I/II clinical trial designed to test safety of CY2301 and its ability to induce a response in HIV-infected patients. The trial is expected to begin in the first quarter of 1997.
Cytel said it aims to develop an immunotherapeutic vaccine to control or eradicate chronic retroviral infection through the induction of virus-specific killer T-cells.

The vaccine uses Cytel's proprietary Theradigm technology and is designed to stimulate a virus-specific cellular immune response against the viral antigen. Cytel said its lead drug candidate in the program is Theradigm-HBV, which is aimed at treating chronic hepatitis B infection.

In Phase I and II clinical trials to date, Theradigm-HBV has stimulated a virus-specific cellular immune response in healthy volunteers and patients infected with hepatitis B. Cytel has said it would initiate clinical studies of Theradigm-HBV in combination with an anti-viral agent in early 1997.
The IND filing is a milestone reached under a $3.3 million AIDS treatment grant from the National Institutes of Health, the company said.
